description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and a third unlabeled chart (likely “hard,” based on context from the paper “Knowledge Crosswords: Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language Models”), each illustrating the distribution of performance across four categories: N–K+, N–K–, N+K–, and N+K+, as defined in the legend. The “easy” chart shows a dominant teal segment (N–K+) at 55.4%, followed by yellow (N–K–) at 38.3%, orange (N+K–) at 4.6%, and a small red (N+K+) slice at 1.7%. The “medium” chart is led by teal (N–K+) at 58.8%, then yellow (N–K–) at 35.4%, orange (N+K–) at 4.0%, and red (N+K+) at 1.8%. The third chart, with no explicit label, shows yellow (N–K–) at 37.3%, orange (N+K–) at 37.9%, teal (N–K+) at 18.1%, and red (N+K+) at 6.7%. All charts include percentage labels within each slice and share a consistent color-coded legend on the right, suggesting a comparison of model behavior across difficulty levels in geometric reasoning tasks.
